hints: Look carefully at what the centre of the Venn diagram means, it is the region shared by chloroplast, mitochondrion and nucleus.
Remember where DNA is found in a plant cell, not just in the nucleus, and ask yourself where mRNA can therefore be made.
walkthrough:
**Recall what transcription needs**

Transcription is making mRNA from a DNA template. So it can only happen where DNA is present.

Think: DNA template + RNA polymerase = mRNA

**Find all the DNA locations in a plant cell**

The nucleus holds the main chromosomal DNA. But mitochondria and chloroplasts both have their own small circular DNA and their own ribosomes.

This is strong evidence they were once free-living prokaryotes.

**Match this to the Venn diagram**

Since all three structures contain DNA, all three carry out transcription to make RNA for their own proteins. That is the overlap of all three circles.

Region D is the only region in the centre shared by chloroplast, mitochondrion and nucleus, so D is the answer.

options.A: Region A is only chloroplast and nucleus. It wrongly leaves out the mitochondrion, which also has DNA and transcribes it.
options.B: Region B is nucleus only. Transcription certainly happens there, but it also happens in mitochondria and chloroplasts.
options.C: Region C is only mitochondrion and nucleus. It wrongly leaves out the chloroplast, which also has DNA and transcribes it.
options.D: Region D is the centre shared by all three circles. Transcription occurs in the nucleus, mitochondrion and chloroplast because all three contain DNA.
